unsafe_site_register.invariant: read_volatile reads the three words of the chip's read-only 96-bit unique ID at 0x0BFA_0700 (design §2.5), in address order, and writes nothing.

unsafe_site_register.invariant: the read-modify-write touches only the RXFLVLM bit of OTG_HS GINTMSK and runs under the critical section every caller holds; the USB driver writes GINTMSK only in its enable, before the device exists.
unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: The pass that chooses the value is host-tested (tests/usb_service.rs, a_full_link_leaves_the_packet_with_the_port); the register write is proved on the bench (S1b-9u).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: OTG_HS is the chip's own register block (PAC 0.16.0). The writes run in bind's critical section, after the build and before the interrupt is unmasked, so DCTL.SDIS, GCCFG and DCFG are never seen half set.
unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: The values written are host-tested (tests/usb_phy.rs: device_mode_gccfg_overrides_vbus_and_keeps_sensing_and_pulldowns_off and full_speed_on_the_hs_phy_sets_dspd_to_one_and_keeps_the_other_fields); the writes are proved on the bench (S1b-9u).

unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: full_speed_on_the_hs_phy_sets_dspd_to_one_and_keeps_the_other_fields pins the value (tests/usb_phy.rs); the write is proved on the bench (S1b-9u).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: the OTG_HS trait values are the chip's: the register block at 0x4204_0000, a 4 KiB FIFO of 1024 words, nine device endpoints, the 160 MHz AHB clock and the on-chip high-speed PHY, driven at full speed with HIGH_SPEED false (design §2.1 and §2.2; PAC DIEPCTL0 to DIEPCTL8).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: the PWR read-modify-writes set only USV (PWR_SVMCR bit 28) and USBPWREN and USBBOOSTEN (PWR_VOSR bits 19 and 20), the USB supply, before the USB core is configured (PAC 0.16.0 field descriptions).
unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: The supply sequence is proved on the bench (S1b-9u); RM0456's USB section owns the order, which is unverified here (design §2.2).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: SYSCFG is the chip's own register block (PAC 0.16.0), and its clock is on since enable; the two writes below touch only OTGHSPHYCR, first CLKSEL and then EN, in ST's order (stm32u5xx_hal.c, lines 1002 and 1030).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: TIM2 is the chip's own timer block at its address (PAC 0.16.0). Only this module uses its registers: Monotonic::start writes them before a wait starts, and the wait and the TIM2 interrupt use them inside the critical section.

unsafe_site_register.invariant: RCC is the chip's own register block (PAC 0.16.0), and the one write sets TIM2EN in RCC_APB1ENR1, the timer's clock.

unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: The lock state and the unlock order are proved on the bench (S1b-9u); the address and slot rules that run before it are host-tested (tests/flash.rs).

unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: The address rule is host-tested (tests/flash.rs a_quad_word_must_be_16_byte_aligned); the programming is proved on the bench (S1b-9u).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: A volatile byte read of the chip's flash at an address that SlotFlash keeps inside the checkpoint slots (slot_address refuses a read past the slot), so the read has no effect on the flash.

unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: The interval rule is host-tested (tests/watchdog.rs, watchdog_interval_gives_prescaler_and_reload). The key order and the counter's start are proved on the bench (S1b-9u).

unsafe_site_register.test_evidence: tests/watchdog.rs pins the code of each interval it lists; the write is proved on the bench (S1b-9u).

unsafe_site_register.invariant: IWDG_RLR takes a 12-bit reload, and timing_for_ms returns at most 4,095 (4,096 counts), so the write leaves the reserved upper bits at zero.
